name: Firefighter
description: Firefighters suppress fires, extricate people from vehicles and structures, handle hazardous materials — and spend most of their calls delivering emergency medical care. ⚠ A Florida median of $58,550, reached through an academy rather than a degree. ⚠⚠⚠ And the thing that actually determines what you earn: in Florida this is a DUAL credential. Departments hire Firefighter/EMTs and Firefighter/Paramedics, several pay for the paramedic programme, and one pays a $10,000 bonus for arriving with both. Plan the EMS half from the start.
credentialNote: ⚠ Florida certifies firefighters under Chapter 633 through the State Fire Marshal's Bureau of Fire Standards and Training, not through a college. The credential is the Minimum Standards course — Firefighter I and Firefighter II — delivered at certified centres including the Florida State Fire College and many state and technical colleges, followed by the state certification examination. ⚠⚠ The federal handbook puts national entry at a postsecondary nondegree award and a high school diploma plus training in emergency medical services, and notes that departments may require EMT certification, with requirements varying by city and state. ⚠⚠⚠ In Florida that variation resolves in one direction: essentially every career department wants EMS. Palm Beach County accepts EMT or paramedic certification at entry; Brevard County hires Firefighter/EMTs and requires them to become paramedic-certified within a set period, providing the tuition; Dunedin pays a one-time $10,000 certification payment at the end of probation to a candidate who arrived holding Firefighter II plus Paramedic. ⚠ No degree is required at any point. Continuing education maintains both credentials.
bodyHtml:
Three roles, and the money is in the second credential

RoleSOC2025 US medianJobsOutlook 2025–35
Firefighter33-2011$59,280355,3004% as fast as average, +13,100
with paramedic certification29-2043✅ paramedic median $60,600, plus department supplements and bonuses——
Fire inspector and investigator33-2021the promotion track — and where a degree starts to count——

⚠⚠⚠ The firefighter median alone understates Florida reality, because the job is not sold alone. This site's Paramedic path found the other half of it: Florida produced 3,661 EMS credentials in one year against roughly 4,900 paramedic openings nationally, and the resolution is that a large share of Florida paramedics are hired as firefighters. These two careers are one labour market here.

⚠⚠ Florida's public-sector pay shape, for the third time

This site found this pattern on schoolteachers, then on police officers. It holds here too, which settles it as a property of Florida public-sector pay rather than of any one profession.

FirefightersFloridaUnited States
10th percentile✅ $37,260$34,910
Median$58,550$59,280
90th percentile⚠ $93,310$101,040

⚠ Florida's floor is $2,350 above the national floor; its ceiling is $7,730 below. The gap is narrower here than in teaching ($30,500) or policing ($16,930), which is itself informative: firefighting is the Florida public-service career where the long-run pay penalty is smallest. Part of the reason is visible in the same table — the 90th percentile is $93,310, well above the median, because overtime, rank and the paramedic supplement all stack.

⚠⚠ For contrast, Florida software developers are below the national figure at BOTH ends. That is an ordinary discount. What teaching, policing and firefighting show is something different: a raised floor and a lowered ceiling. Florida public service starts people well and tops out early.

⚠⚠⚠ Plan the EMS credential first, or at least alongside

The single most consequential decision on this page is not which academy to attend; it is whether you arrive with EMS certification.

You arrive withWhat happens
Firefighter II only⚠ a narrower set of departments will consider you
Firefighter II + EMT✅ the standard hire at most Florida departments
Firefighter II + Paramedic✅✅ the preferred hire — and at Dunedin, a $10,000 payment at the end of probation

⚠ And note the route Brevard County describes, because it is a genuinely good deal: they hire Firefighter/EMTs, require them to become paramedic-certified within a departmental timeframe, and provide the tuition. If you cannot afford the paramedic programme up front, that is the route to look for — get hired at EMT level, let the department pay for the upgrade.

⚠⚠ Take the EMT course for COLLEGE CREDIT if you can. This site's Paramedic path found that Florida runs the same EMT training two ways: as college-credit EMS 1119 at 19 institutions and as a 300-clock-hour PSAV course, EMS 0110, at 19 others. Both reach the same NREMT examination; only one counts toward the associate degree you will want for promotion.

⚠⚠ The degree is for rank, and it comes later

Florida awards 1,955 fire protection credentials a year at 36 public institutions — and 1,714 of them are short certificates, which is the academy. Only 156 associate degrees and 43 bachelor's.

⚠ That ratio is the clearest statement of how this career works. Nobody needs a degree to be hired. Lieutenant, captain, battalion chief, fire marshal and inspector roles increasingly expect one — and departments frequently pay for it once you are employed, on a schedule that fits a 24-on, 48-off rota far better than it fits a school-leaver's finances.

⚠⚠ So the sequence that works is: academy, EMS, hired, then the degree on the department's time and money. Doing it in the other order is not wrong, but it spends your own money on the part the employer would have funded.

What the work actually is

The federal handbook describes academy training in firefighting and fire-prevention techniques, local building codes and emergency medical procedures, followed by a probationary period. What it does not convey is the proportion.

⚠⚠ Most calls are medical. A modern career firefighter spends far more time on chest pain, falls, overdoses and vehicle collisions than on structure fires — which is exactly why the EMS credential has become the hiring gate. If the medical side does not appeal, this is the wrong career, and finding that out before the academy is worth a great deal.

⚠ And be clear about the rest: a 24-hour shift rota that wrecks ordinary sleep, cumulative exposure to trauma, documented occupational cancer risk from combustion products, and a physical standard you must maintain for thirty years rather than pass once.

Necessary skills

  • Sustained physical capacity, in heat, in gear, under air. The academy tests it; the career requires you to keep it.
  • Emergency medical competence, because that is the majority of the work.
  • Working inside a command structure under conditions where arguing is not available.
  • Mechanical and spatial reasoning — building construction, forcible entry, ventilation, where a fire will go next.
  • Calm in other people's catastrophes, repeatedly, for decades.
  • Deliberate recovery. Sleep, mental health and cancer screening are occupational requirements in this job, not optional extras.

Advice

⚠⚠ Get EMT certified before or alongside the fire academy, and take it for college credit where you can. It is the difference between being a candidate and being the preferred candidate.

⚠ Ask every target department three questions: do you require paramedic at hire or within a period; do you pay for it; and is there a certification bonus. The answers vary enormously between neighbouring Florida departments and are worth tens of thousands of dollars.

⚠ Leave the degree until you are hired. 1,714 certificates against 199 degrees a year is the profession telling you the order. The degree matters for rank, and departments fund it.

⚠ Look at the 90th percentile, not just the median. $93,310 in Florida against a $58,550 median is a wide spread, and it is reachable through rank, overtime and the paramedic supplement rather than through luck.

And ride along before you commit. Most Florida departments will arrange it. A single shift will tell you more about whether the medical calls, the sleep disruption and the waiting suit you than any amount of reading — and this is a career people stay in for thirty years or leave in three.

cipCodes.note: ⚠⚠ Allied health, and specifically emergency medical services — not an adjacent field but effectively half of this job. Most Florida career departments hire dual-certified Firefighter/EMTs or Firefighter/Paramedics, and 39 Florida public institutions teach EMS.

Criminal justice and corrections — the other public-safety academy, taught at 46 Florida public institutions and frequently in the same college division. Named because candidates routinely weigh the two against each other.

programs.note: The programme itself — 36 Florida public institutions and 1,955 credentials, of which 1,714 are the Minimum Standards academy. ⚠ Read its degrees note: the academy gets you hired, the degree gets you promoted, and departments often pay for the second.

⚠⚠ Not an adjacent programme — effectively a requirement. Florida departments hire dual-certified, Brevard pays the paramedic tuition for its Firefighter/EMTs and Dunedin pays $10,000 for arriving with Firefighter II plus Paramedic. ⚠ Take the EMT course for COLLEGE CREDIT (EMS1119) rather than clock hours (EMS0110) if a degree is anywhere in your plan.

⚠ Not a route here — separate academy, separate certification, no transfer. Named because it is the alternative most candidates consider, often at the same college. Policing pays a higher Florida median ($74,470 against $58,550); firefighting has the paramedic supplement, a wider top end and a different schedule.

courses.reason: Emergency Medical Technician — 19 institutions, the most widely carried EMS course in the state. ⚠⚠ The credential that decides whether a Florida department will consider you, and the first half of the dual certification every career department wants.
courses.variantNote: ⚠⚠⚠ Take THIS rather than EMS0110 if there is any chance you will want the associate degree for promotion. Both reach the same NREMT examination and the same Florida certification; only EMS1119 is college credit. ⚠ EMS0110 is the 300-clock-hour PSAV version, also at 19 institutions, and it carries none.

courses.reason: Emergency Medical Technician Laboratory — 17 institutions. The practical half: airways, immobilisation, extrication and the skills stations.
EMT Hospital and Field Experience — 9 institutions. The first supervised shifts in an emergency department and on an ambulance.
courses.variantNote: ⚠⚠ A clinical course on the host service's roster, including nights and weekends. Background screening, immunisations and current certifications must be complete BEFORE the first shift.

courses.reason: Paramedic, modules 1–3 — 7 institutions. The start of the paramedic programme, which is the credential Florida departments pay bonuses for and often fund.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Florida numbers the same national paramedic curriculum as three courses (EMS2603/2604/2605) or two (EMS2601/2602). ⚠⚠ If a department will fund this after hiring, that is usually the better financial order — get hired at EMT level first.

courses.reason: Paramedic Field Internship — 11 institutions, the terminal requirement of the paramedic credential and where most attrition happens.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Florida requires the field internship to be aboard an ADVANCED LIFE SUPPORT permitted ambulance. Very hard to combine with full-time work — which is another argument for letting a department fund and schedule it.

courses.reason: Introduction to Fire Science — the profession, its organisation, fire behaviour and the incident command system. The usual first course of a Florida fire science degree.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Distinct from the Minimum Standards academy, which is a state certification course rather than a college course. The degree and the certification are two different things.

courses.reason: Fire Prevention Practices — codes, inspections and the prevention side that becomes the fire inspector and fire marshal promotion track.
Building Construction for the Fire Service — how buildings behave and fail in fire, which is what determines whether an interior attack is survivable.
Company Officer — supervision, tactics and command at the first promotion level. ⚠ This is the sort of course the degree exists for, and the sort a department will pay for once you are hired.
Firefighting Tactics and Strategy — size-up, resource deployment and fireground decision-making.
Anatomy and Physiology I — 20 institutions. Required by the paramedic route, and the science behind the majority of calls you will actually run.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Two equivalent packagings: BSC2085 plus BSC2085L at 20 institutions, combined BSC2085C at 7. ⚠⚠ Required for the paramedic associate degree rather than for the fire academy — another reason to take the EMS side for credit.

courses.reason: English Composition I — 39 institutions. Incident reports, patient care reports and investigation notes are legal documents, and the patient care report is a medical record.
Interpersonal Communication — 16 institutions. Most calls involve frightened people in their own homes, and how you speak to them is most of what they remember.
Introduction to Psychology — 33 institutions. Crisis behaviour, mental health calls and — not incidentally — understanding the cumulative effect of the work on yourself.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Deliberate recovery is an occupational requirement in this career rather than a personal preference. Programmes that discuss it openly are better programmes.
